note: Sioux County Conservation's first park (1961): 11 acres north of Alton at old Hwy 60 and Hwy 10, with a fishing pond, open and enclosed shelters, a playground, a disc golf course and seasonal modern restrooms. Park hours 7 am - 10:30 pm. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: 4 sites with 30/20-amp electric, $10 a night, dump and water fill, open mid-April to mid-October. It is a county park with designated campsites, not a bare pull-off. Sites aren't identifiable on imagery, so fit is unconfirmed.
flags: CAMPGROUND vs PULL-OFF: it's a small county-park campground. Sioux County Conservation lists 'four (4) camp sites' with 30/20-amp electric, a fee, a dump station and a water hydrant, and a mid-April to mid-October camping season, inside an 11-acre park with shelters, restrooms and a pond. That is more than a highway overnight pull-off, so it passes. Google: 4.4 stars from 101 reviews.

FIT / CAVEAT (lead): no lengths, pads or layout are posted, and on NAIP I can't tell which spots are the four sites. Candidates are a small gravel loop under trees east of the pond, off Hwy 10, at about 42.99605,-96.00591, and a gravel lot off old Hwy 60 to the north. There is no clear limit, so per AWH 2026-11-02 it stays. Proposed caveat for the note: 'Site size not posted: four electric sites, layout unconfirmed.' Proposed only, not written into the note.

BOOKING: the pages don't say whether the sites are reservable. The county's mycountyparks listing has no campsite facilities to book, only the shelter, which points to walk-up, but it isn't stated. No booking group was written.

WATERFRONT: not waterfront stands. The pond is given as '5 acre', right at the ~5-acre pond line. The candidate camp loop is separated from it by a 15-40 m tree belt, and the Floyd River runs southwest beyond woods.

PIN: the stored 42.99429,-96.00745 is in trees south of the enclosed-shelter pad, about 215 m from the candidate camp loop (42.99605,-96.00591). That's under the 250 m line, so no correction is required, but it isn't on a site. Google's park pin is 42.99585,-96.00579.

PHONE (missing): the entry has none. The Sioux County Conservation office is (712) 552-1047, from the county's mycountyparks page. Google gives +1 712-756-4370 for the park, which I haven't matched to an operator page. Website: the mycountyparks park page is the operator's, fine as stored.
